attributes.description: Distribution opsdir-adapter-hashicorp-vault (import opsdir_adapter_hashicorp_vault), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:hashicorp-vault; depends on opsdir.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["Vault CLI (1.11+ for -mount; pinned 2.2.0 for the vault marker tests)", "Vault HTTP API v1 (PKI secrets engine: issuers, roles, certs, cert, config; sys/policies/acl), GET only", "opsdir-adapter-x509 (certificate_facts; cryptography)"]
attributes.purpose: HashiCorp Vault secret store: resolves vault:// references (owns the vault scheme); inventories its KV mounts, metadata only (importer hashicorp-vault/kv-metadata from `vault kv list` / `vault kv metadata get` output; collector running them with the operator's login, VAULT_ADDR from the store's ciamStoreEndpoint; inventory_locator mount/path). Reads Vault PKI mounts into the core pki domain (importer hashicorp-vault/pki, pki.py: CA per mount named after its default issuer's CN, AIA endpoints, roles as the CA's own templates via roles.py and ACL-policy enrollment via policies.py, the certificates Vault keeps parsed with opsdir-adapter-x509's certificate_facts; GET-only collector pki_collect.py per ciamCollectionSource naming a mount, X-Vault-Token/Bearer from the credential reference; scripts/export-vault-pki.sh for large mounts).

attributes.description: HashiCorp Vault PKI mounts read into the core pki domain by the hashicorp-vault adapter (importer hashicorp-vault/pki), metadata only. A GET-only collector per collection source naming a mount (X-Vault-Token/Bearer from the credential reference, never stored) lists issuers, roles, certificates and the ACL policies (optional), reads each item and five config answers, trimmed; scripts/export-vault-pki.sh writes the same export for large mounts. The importer (pure) makes the mount one CA named after its default issuer's CN (else the mount), its revocation endpoints from the issuer's AIA overrides else config/urls (template variables filled or kept), each role a CA-scoped template '<CA>/<role>' (ciamTemplateAuthority: validity, usages, requester-named subject, no approval, the policies granting issue/sign, broad via default) and the certificates Vault keeps parsed by opsdir-adapter-x509's certificate_facts; the inventory is complete only for what Vault keeps (incomplete for no_store roles, unread certificates, a missing listing; denied when refused). Vault records no revocation reason, role or requester per certificate.

attributes.name: template_entry
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "name", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "display", "type": "str|None", "required": false}, {"name": "oid", "type": "str|None", "required": false}, {"name": "max_days", "type": "int|None", "required": false}, {"name": "usages", "type": "tuple[str]", "required": false}, {"name": "rights", "type": "dict|None", "required": false, "description": "{attribute of TEMPLATE_RIGHTS: value, or a tuple for ciamEnrollee}"}, {"name": "authority", "type": "str|None", "required": false, "description": "the CA name whose own template it is; None for a directory-wide template"}]
attributes.purpose: A certificate template's entry (its purpose and renewal owner, the operator's, kept): display name, OID, the longest validity it issues in days, its extended key usages, its rights (what it lets requesters do and who may request from it; None: not read) and, for a CA-scoped template, the CA whose own it is (ciamTemplateAuthority).

attributes.name: templates_group
attributes.purpose: An Imported group: ou=certificate-templates made exactly these directory-wide templates (AD CS's forest list), the record's container and every CA-scoped template (ciamTemplateAuthority) kept; a directory template gone leaves the record.

attributes.name: certificate_facts
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "pem", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "PEM text whose first certificate is read"}]
attributes.purpose: The public facts of a PEM certificate as the record writes them, CA-neutral (any CA's issued-certificate importer): serial (lowercase even-length hex), SHA-256 fingerprint (colon upper-case hex, ciamFingerprint's form), subject and issuer (RFC 4514), validity (GeneralizedTime) and extended key usages (OIDs; None when the certificate has no EKU extension); None when the text isn't a certificate. Never a key.
attributes.returns: {"type": "dict | None", "description": "{serial, sha256, subject, issuer, not_before, not_after, usages} or None"}

attributes.name: is_ca_scoped
attributes.purpose: Whether a certificate template is one CA's own (it records ciamTemplateAuthority), not one a directory shares with every CA.

attributes.name: ca_templates_groups
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true, "description": "the record"}, {"name": "authority", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the CA's name (cn under ou=certificate-authorities)"}, {"name": "templates", "type": "tuple[Entry]", "required": true, "description": "the CA's template entries (template_entry with authority)"}]
attributes.purpose: Imported groups making the CA named authority's own templates exactly these: one group per template made as given, and an empty group (it leaves the record) for each template the record holds as that CA's (ciamTemplateAuthority) that it no longer has; every other template, directory-wide or another CA's, kept.

attributes.name: policy_rules
attributes.purpose: ((path, capabilities), ...) of a Vault ACL policy's text, HCL (path blocks found by a brace-depth scan outside strings and comments; nested blocks such as allowed_parameters allowed) or JSON; the legacy policy = "read|write|deny|sudo" form as its capabilities; None when a block is unclosed.

attributes.name: path_matches
attributes.purpose: Whether a Vault policy path pattern covers a request path: + one whole segment, a trailing * any rest, a templated {{...}} segment any one segment.

attributes.name: path_priority
attributes.purpose: Sort key of a policy path among those matching one request (highest applies), Vault's priority rules in order: first + or * later, not ending in *, fewer + segments, longer, lexically larger.

attributes.name: grants
attributes.purpose: Whether one policy's rules give a request path any of the wanted capabilities (default create/update): the merged capabilities of its highest-priority matching paths, unless they deny.

attributes.name: role_paths
attributes.purpose: The request paths that issue or sign from a PKI role: <mount>/issue|sign/<role>, and through each issuer reference given <mount>/issuer/<ref>/issue|sign/<role>.

attributes.name: verbatim_paths
attributes.purpose: The request paths signing any request whatever the roles allow (sign-verbatim, with or without a role, through each issuer reference).

attributes.name: granting
attributes.purpose: The names of the policies ({name: rules}) granting any of the request paths, root and unread ones left out, in name order.

attributes.name: enrollment
attributes.purpose: (enrollees, scope, why) of a role reached at these request paths: 'policy <name>' per granting policy; broad when default grants it, restricted otherwise; unknown with why when the policies weren't read (None) or one couldn't be read.

attributes.name: seconds
attributes.purpose: A Vault duration (integer seconds, its text, or 72h/30m/1d via the core's duration_seconds) in seconds, or None.

attributes.name: max_validity_days
attributes.purpose: (whole days rounded up of a role's max_ttl, or None; why not, or None): 0 or none is the mount's maximum, which the role doesn't say.

attributes.name: role_usages
attributes.purpose: (the extended key usage OIDs a role puts in its certificates: its server/client/code-signing/email flags, its ext_key_usage Go names, its ext_key_usage_oids; the names it doesn't know).

attributes.name: subject_from_request
attributes.purpose: Whether a role lets the requester name the subject: always, unless every allowed name is templated from the requester's identity (allowed_domains_template, only {{identity...}} domains, not allow_any_name).

attributes.name: answer_data
attributes.purpose: The data of a Vault answer (its JSON envelope's data, or a bare object), or None.

attributes.name: listing
attributes.purpose: The keys of a Vault listing (the CLI's bare array, or an answer's data.keys), or None when it isn't one.

attributes.name: file_name
attributes.purpose: A listed key as the export file holding its answer is named (a serial's colons as dashes).

attributes.name: mounts
attributes.purpose: The PKI mounts an export holds (each with its pki/<mount>/issuers.json), in order; a mount's own config/issuers.json is never taken for a mount <mount>/config.

attributes.name: aia_endpoints
attributes.purpose: ((kind, n, url, template or None), ...) of the URLs an issuer writes into what it issues: its own AIA fields when it sets any, else the mount's config/urls; {{issuer_id}}/{{cluster_path}}/{{cluster_aia_path}} filled when templating is on, an unfilled one kept with its template.

attributes.name: issued_facts
attributes.purpose: The ciamIssuedCertificate facts of a Vault certificate answer from its public PEM (certificate_facts) and its revocation (time; reason unspecified, Vault records none), or None when it holds no certificate.

attributes.name: read_mount
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "mount", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "get", "type": "callable", "required": true, "description": "name -> the mount's file text or None"}, {"name": "when", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "GeneralizedTime of the inventory"}]
attributes.purpose: (Imported groups, notices) of one PKI mount: its CA (named after the default issuer's CN, else the mount) with its revocation endpoints, its issued-certificate inventory (complete for what Vault keeps; incomplete for unread certificates, a missing listing, no_store or unread roles; denied when refused) and its roles as the CA's own templates (ca_templates_groups).

attributes.name: read_pki
attributes.purpose: Importer hashicorp-vault/pki read(): per mount in the export its CA with revocation endpoints, its issued-certificate inventory and its roles as the CA's own templates, each replacing the record's; refused without --at.

attributes.name: trimmed
attributes.purpose: A Request keep function: a Vault answer reduced to {"data": the given fields of its data}; text that isn't one kept as it is.

attributes.name: credential
attributes.purpose: The Request credential sending a collection source's Vault token: X-Vault-Token (scheme api-key), else Authorization: Bearer; None without a credential.

attributes.name: mount_of
attributes.purpose: (Vault's address, the mount) a source location https://<vault>:<port>/<mount> names, or None.

attributes.name: pki_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps for hashicorp-vault/pki: per readable source's mount, the issuers/roles/certs listings, five config reads and the ACL policy listing (optional, 403/404 nothing), then each issuer, role, certificate and policy the listings name; GETs only, answers trimmed.

attributes.name: source_problems
attributes.purpose: Why hashicorp-vault/pki collection sources can't be read: their own problems, a credential scheme other than api-key/bearer, a location naming no mount.

attributes.name: listing
attributes.purpose: Bash: save a Vault listing (vault list -format=json) as a file and print its keys; an empty listing saves nothing; with optional, a refused one too; any other failure aborts.

attributes.name: answer
attributes.purpose: Bash: save one vault read -format=json answer as a file; with optional, a missing or refused one saves nothing; else the failure aborts.

attributes.name: issue_label
attributes.purpose: How a finding or report names a certificate an inventory holds: `request <id>` when its cn is a request id (AD CS), else `serial <serial>` (a CA naming them by serial, Vault).

attributes.description: Milestone 108 item (e) of analysis note 3068, non-cloud CAs only (worker). The pki domain's authorities / issued-certificate inventory / revocation endpoints (flow 60) are CA-neutral and AD CS fills them today (flow 61). Read other CAs into the same model, metadata only, never keys: HashiCorp Vault PKI secrets engine (issuers, roles as templates, certificate list/serials, CRL/OCSP config; in opsdir-adapter-hashicorp-vault or a new package, decide at design), EJBCA (REST v1/v2: CAs, certificate profiles, certificate search) and Venafi / CyberArk Certificate Manager (TPP/TLS Protect: certificates, policy folders, issuing templates). Read-only collectors with least privilege, saved-export importers, matching rules unchanged. Research each current API and edition (incl. any FedRAMP/government offering) via Codex first; propose in the design gate which of the three to build now and which to defer. Cloud private CAs (AWS Private CA, Azure Key Vault certificates, Google CAS) wait until task 557's merge (same cloud adapters); DoD PKI/ECA partner trust stays for later.
